segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Since many have undertaken to compile an account of the events that have been fulfilled among us,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: just as they were handed down to us by those who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and became servants of the word,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: it seemed good to me also, having followed everything carefully from the start, to write it out for you in order, most excellent Theophilus,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: so that you may know the certainty of the things you have been taught.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In the days of Herod, king of Judea, there was a priest named Zechariah, of the division of Abijah. His wife was from the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Both of them were righteous before God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and righteous requirements of the Lord.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But they had no child, because Elizabeth was barren, and both were far along in their days.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now it happened that, while he was serving as priest before God in the turn of his division,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: he was chosen by lot, according to the custom of the priesthood, to enter the sanctuary of the Lord and burn incense.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The whole multitude of the people was praying outside at the hour of the incense offering.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then an angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing to the right of the altar of incense.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Zechariah was troubled when he saw him, and fear fell upon him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But the angel said to him,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you are to name him John.

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: You will have joy and delight, and many will rejoice at his birth,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: for he will be great before the Lord. He is never to drink wine or beer, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother’s womb.

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: He will turn many of the children of Israel back to the Lord their God.

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: And he will go on before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of fathers to their children and the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous, to make ready for the Lord a people prepared.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Zechariah said to the angel,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “How will I know this? For I am an old man, and my wife is far along in her days.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The angel answered him,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “I am Gabriel, who stands before God, and I was sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: And look, you will be silent and unable to speak until the day these things happen, because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled in their proper time.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Meanwhile the people were waiting for Zechariah and were amazed at how long he was staying in the sanctuary.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he came out he could not speak to them, and they realised that he had seen a vision in the sanctuary. He kept making signs to them and remained mute.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the days of his service were completed, he went back to his home.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After those days his wife Elizabeth conceived, and she kept herself hidden for five months, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “This is what the Lord has done for me in the days when he looked upon me to take away my disgrace among people.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a town in Galilee named Nazareth,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: to a virgin betrothed to a man named Joseph, of the house of David. The virgin’s name was Mary.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He came in to her and said,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “Greetings, favoured one! The Lord is with you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But she was deeply troubled at his words and pondered what kind of greeting this might be.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The angel said to her,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “Do not be afraid, Mary, for you have found favour with God.

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: And look, you will conceive in your womb and bear a son, and you are to name him Jesus.

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: He will be great and will be called Son of the Most High, and the Lord God will give him the throne of his father David,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and his kingdom will have no end.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Mary said to the angel,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “How will this be, since I have not slept with a man?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The angel answered her,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. Therefore the child to be born will be called holy, Son of God.

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: And look, your relative Elizabeth has herself conceived a son in her old age, and this is the sixth month for her who was called barren.

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: For no word from God will be powerless.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Mary said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Here I am, the Lord’s slave. May it happen to me according to your word.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then the angel left her.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In those days Mary set out and went in haste to the hill country, to a town of Judah,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and she entered the house of Zechariah and greeted Elizabeth.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the baby leapt in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: She cried out in a loud voice and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And why should this happen to me, that the mother of my Lord comes to me?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: For look, when the sound of your greeting reached my ears, the baby in my womb leapt with delight.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And blessed is she who believed that what was spoken to her from the Lord would be fulfilled.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Mary said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “My soul proclaims the greatness of the Lord,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: and my spirit delights in God my Saviour,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: for he has taken notice of the lowliness of his slave. For look, from now on all generations will call me blessed,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: for the Mighty One has done great things for me, and holy is his name,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: and his mercy is on those who fear him, from generation to generation.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: He has done a mighty deed with his arm; he has scattered those who are proud in the thoughts of their hearts.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: He has brought down rulers from their thrones and lifted up the lowly;

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: he has filled the hungry with good things and sent the rich away empty.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: He has helped Israel his servant, remembering mercy,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: just as he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and his offspring forever.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Mary stayed with her about three months and then returned to her home.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now the time came for Elizabeth to give birth, and she bore a son.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Her neighbours and relatives heard that the Lord had shown great mercy to her, and they rejoiced with her.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: On the eighth day they came to circumcise the child, and they were going to call him Zechariah, after his father.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But his mother spoke up and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “No! He is to be called John.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They said to her,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “There is no one among your relatives who is called by that name.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they made signs to his father, asking what he would want him to be called.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He asked for a writing tablet and wrote,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “John is his name.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they were all amazed.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At once his mouth was opened and his tongue set free, and he began to speak, blessing God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Fear came over all who lived around them, and all these things were talked about throughout the hill country of Judea.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: All who heard them stored them in their hearts, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “What then will this child be?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For indeed the hand of the Lord was with him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: His father Zechariah was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, for he has visited his people and worked redemption for them,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: and has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of David his servant,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: just as he spoke through the mouth of his holy prophets from of old:

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate us;

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: to show mercy to our fathers and to remember his holy covenant,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: the oath he swore to Abraham our father, to grant us

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: that we, rescued from the hand of enemies, might serve him without fear

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: in holiness and righteousness before him all our days.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And you, child, will be called a prophet of the Most High, for you will go before the Lord to prepare his ways,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: to give his people knowledge of salvation through the forgiveness of their sins,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: because of the tender mercy of our God, by which the dawn from on high will visit us,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: to shine on those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The child grew and became strong in spirit, and he was in the wilderness until the day of his public appearance to Israel.

notes.traditional: most surely believed (KJV); fulfilled or accomplished (most modern versions)
notes.note: The verb can mean to bring something to completion or to convince someone fully. Most scholars take it here of events brought to completion, with the overtone that God's purposes were being carried out in them. The older rendering ‘most surely believed’ takes it in the second sense.

The priests were organised into twenty-four hereditary divisions (1 Chronicles 24), of which Abijah's was the eighth. Each division served at the temple for a week at a time, twice a year. Because there were many priests, duties such as offering the incense were assigned by lot, as in verse 9.

The Greek word belongs to the same family as ‘righteous’ earlier in the verse, and the rendering keeps that link visible. In the Septuagint it regularly refers to God's statutes, so ‘ordinances’ is not wrong. Greek has a single word-family where English divides between righteous/just and righteousness/justice.

Greek distinguishes the sanctuary building itself, which only priests entered, from the whole temple complex with its courts, for which a different word is used. The people praying ‘outside’ in verse 10 are in the courts, still within the temple in the wider sense. Most English versions use ‘temple’ for both words.

The Greek word is borrowed from a Semitic term for fermented drinks other than grape wine, chiefly grain-based beer. ‘Strong drink’ now suggests distilled spirits, which were unknown in antiquity; some versions use ‘other fermented drink’. The wording echoes the Nazirite vow in Numbers 6:3 and the instructions about Samson in Judges 13.

The Greek word can mean mute, deaf, or both. Verse 20 mentions only the loss of speech, and the rendering follows that. But verse 62, where people make signs to Zechariah, suggests he could not hear either.

notes.traditional: Hail, full of grace; Hail, thou that art highly favoured
notes.note: The first word was the ordinary Greek greeting, though it literally means ‘rejoice’, and some scholars hear that sense here. The second is a passive form meaning one to whom favour has been shown, and it chimes in sound with the greeting. ‘Full of grace’ comes from the Latin version; most modern translations render it much as here.

notes.phrase: since I have not slept with a man
notes.traditional: seeing I know not a man; since I am a virgin
notes.note: The Greek says literally ‘since I do not know a man’, using the biblical idiom in which ‘know’ refers to sexual intercourse. The present tense describes her current state. The rendering replaces the Hebrew idiom with an equivalent English one.

notes.phrase: will be called holy, Son of God
notes.traditional: that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God (KJV)
notes.note: The Greek can be construed in two ways: ‘the child to be born will be called holy, Son of God’ or ‘the holy one to be born will be called Son of God’. The rendering follows the punctuation of the Greek edition translated here. Scholars are divided, and the difference in meaning is slight.

notes.phrase: no word from God will be powerless
notes.traditional: For nothing will be impossible with God
notes.note: The Greek noun means ‘word’ but, under Hebrew influence, can also mean ‘thing’. The sentence echoes Genesis 18:14 in the Septuagint, where it is usually understood as ‘thing’, and most versions render accordingly here. This translation keeps ‘word’ because the text has ‘from God’ and because Mary takes up the same noun in the next verse; both readings are defensible.

This is the ordinary Greek word for a female slave, and most versions soften it to ‘servant’ or ‘handmaid’. In the Septuagint, people use it of themselves when speaking humbly to God, as Hannah does in 1 Samuel 1:11, which Mary's song echoes in verse 48. It expresses belonging wholly to a master and readiness to obey, not degradation.

notes.phrase: blessed is she who believed that
notes.traditional: blessed is she who believed that (or: for) there would be a fulfilment
notes.note: The Greek conjunction can mean ‘that’ or ‘because’, so the sentence may also be read ‘blessed is she who believed, for what was spoken to her will be fulfilled’. Most translations choose ‘that’. The word for ‘blessed’ here is a different Greek word from the one in verse 42: this one pronounces someone to be in an enviable state, the other speaks of being blessed by God.

In the Hebrew Scriptures an animal's horn is a standing image of strength, and Psalm 132:17 speaks of God making a horn grow for David. The phrase means a powerful deliverer, here one from David's royal line.

Some of the earliest manuscripts have the future tense, which the Greek edition translated here adopts. The majority of later manuscripts have the past tense, matching verse 68, and the King James Version follows them. Most modern editions prefer the future.

notes.traditional: the dayspring from on high; the rising sun
notes.note: The Greek word means a rising, usually of the sun or a star, and the image of light in verse 79 supports ‘dawn’. In the Septuagint the same word also translates the Hebrew for ‘branch’ or ‘shoot’, a title for the coming Davidic king (Jeremiah 23:5; Zechariah 3:8; 6:12). Many scholars think both associations are in play.

candidates.reason: Needs a fixed distinction from ἱερόν (temple complex) across the Gospels, Acts, Paul's temple imagery and Revelation, where most versions use 'temple' for both.
The δοῦλος word-group recurs throughout the New Testament, and the choice between 'slave' and 'servant' should be made once, including its contrast with παῖς and διάκονος.
Translators divide between 'grace' and 'favour'; the register should fix when each is used so that readers can track the word from the Gospels into Paul.

candidates.rendering: forever (εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας, εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα); of old (ἀπ’ αἰῶνος)
candidates.reason: The 'age' vocabulary and its fixed phrases, together with αἰώνιος, recur in nearly every book, and renderings vary between 'forever', 'eternal' and 'age'.
The verb and its noun εὐαγγέλιον are rendered variously as 'preach the gospel', 'bring good news' and 'evangelise', and should be consistent across Luke-Acts and Paul.
